routing.reason: One optional field added through a new migration, API validation, a small page change, tests and README, all in one small codebase with clear acceptance criteria.
rulings: Ruling: default workflow — a feature with a plan gate suits it and this is not an urgent fix — cost if wrong: a slightly slower run
Ruling: skip `frame` — the ticket already gives six testable acceptance criteria and the behaviour is unambiguous — cost if wrong: a missed edge case surfaces at review

Ruling: leave `prd`, `architecture`, `ux`, `seo` off — no vague scope, no cross-cutting decision, the UI change is one date input and a label on an existing page, and no public SEO pages are involved — cost if wrong: a plain-looking date field

Ruling: security review at medium effort — one new user-supplied input to parse and store, but parameterized SQL and strict date validation keep the risk low — cost if wrong: a validation gap caught late
Ruling: plan at low effort — a single-module change over src/db.ts, src/tasks.ts, src/app.ts, public/, test/ and README.md — cost if wrong: a thinner plan the lead must redo

Ruling: the new migration is appended to `migrations` in src/db.ts as `ALTER TABLE tasks ADD COLUMN due_date TEXT` (nullable, no default, so existing rows read NULL) and the shipped one is never edited; the existing `migrations` review step covers it — cost if wrong: a broken upgrade of existing databases

Ruling: date validation checks that the string matches `^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$` and is a real calendar day (rejects 2026-02-30), without time-zone conversion — cost if wrong: an off-by-one day if a Date round-trip is used
Ruling: budget $1.20 — an S change with one implementer and the standard review steps — cost if wrong: TermF asks the user before spending more

criteria.why: Task interface/Row gain due_date; column nullable so default null; SELECT * returns it everywhere.
POST passes due_date ?? null; PATCH only sets it when key present, null clears, absent keeps (updateTask undefined check).
isValidDueDate checks regex plus UTC round-trip; validation precedes any write and returns the exact error message on POST and PATCH.
New ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN migration appended; existing rows get NULL; a test migrates an old user_version=1 DB.
Page renders a <time> element next to the title when due_date is set, and the form has an optional date input.
Tests cover default, create, patch set/keep/clear, invalid values, leap day, 404 and migration; README documents the field.

findings.what: Submit handler now wraps the call in try/catch and shows errors. This is reasonable, since the server can now return 400, but it goes slightly beyond the ticket.
The POST table row has a double space before `201, the task`.

`"due_date" in body` throws a TypeError if the JSON body is `null` or a primitive. Malformed JSON also throws from readJson. Whether these become a 500 depends on the existing error handler, which is not in the diff. It is a new path for a null body on POST/PATCH.
There are no tests for the UI, and none for a `due_date: null` on POST. Validation is only tested through the API.
Years like 0000 or 0050 pass the regex. Date.UTC maps years 0–99 to 1900+, so the round-trip check rejects them. This is acceptable behaviour, though accidental.

judge.summary: The change meets all six criteria. It validates strictly before any write, adds a proper migration, and has thorough tests, including a migration test. The flaws are minor: a stray whitespace typo in app.js, a double space in the README, and a possible TypeError when the request body is `null`.
